content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text resolves an Isaiah 7:14 chain link by noting that the sign itself does not state the mechanism, which is a verse-level stating test rather than a chain-against-chain weighing by footing.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the sign itself does not state the mechanism", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "never verse by verse — I weighed (A) a bar on using any single verse's failure to state the mechanism as decisive, versus (B) a bar only on demanding that a verse explicitly state the contrary. The judge's use of the sign's silence is a verse-level stating test under either reading.", "why": "The judge says the sign itself does not state the mechanism, using a single verse's silence as a stating-verse test to make the link underdetermined instead of weighing the competing chains by footing as K-C requires."}
